headline: High: Chatwoot’s broad egress and customer-data handling create leakage and compliance risk; the pair’s interaction is otherwise mostly unconnected.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-nlp is non-runnable and has no shared channel or I/O surfaces, while chatwoot exposes API integrations and broad egress. A prompt-injection pathway is therefore not default, but if an operator manually copies content from chatwoot into awesome-nlp workflows, injected text could be reinterpreted. The pairwise interaction is weakly evidenced, so uncertainty stays low rather than none.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies chatwoot messages into an NLP workflow that parses instructions, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared file or clipboard bridge is introduced, chatwoot content can reach awesome-nlp without provenance checks.
mitigations: Disable manual copy-paste between systems for untrusted text.
Add a fixed delimiter and instruction-stripping preprocessor.
Review any shared clipboard or file-sync setup.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, and it has broad network egress. awesome-nlp is non-runnable and shows no data surfaces, so the main leakage risk is one-way from chatwoot into external services or logs, not from the pair symmetrically. Because sensitive customer data is in scope and egress is default, medium is warranted.
conditions: IF chatwoot sends customer messages or profiles to external integrations, those data classes can leave the local boundary.
IF an operator routes chatwoot exports into any downstream NLP service, customer data may be exposed.
mitigations: Audit enabled integrations in chatwoot.
Disable unused outbound connectors.
Redact customer identifiers before export.
Restrict logs to non-sensitive fields.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on outbound payloads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp is non-runnable and has no write or network permissions, while chatwoot’s profile shows integrations but no shared mutable resource with awesome-nlp. There is no documented overlapping filesystem, git, database, or OAuth scope, so a write-conflict pathway is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF both agents are later given write access to the same directory or database, conflict risk would need reevaluation.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces.
Avoid granting shared write access.
Document any future shared resource before deployment.

D_cascading_error.rationale: chatwoot can act on integrations and customer workflows, but awesome-nlp is non-runnable and does not produce authoritative outputs in this profile. That makes a direct A-to-B automation chain unlikely by default. If an operator nevertheless feeds awesome-nlp-generated text into chatwoot actions, errors could cascade, but the blast radius is limited and requires manual wiring.
conditions: IF awesome-nlp output is manually treated as authoritative input to chatwoot workflows, downstream mistakes can propagate.
IF chatwoot automations are configured to act on imported NLP text without review, cascading errors become possible.
mitigations: Require human review before chatwoot actions.
Label imported NLP text as untrusted.
Disable auto-action rules on imported content.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before outbound actions.

E_compliance.rationale: chatwoot clearly touches customer data and messages, which can carry privacy and retention obligations, while awesome-nlp is an open-source list with no data classes touched and no runnable surface. The pair itself does not prove a residency mismatch, but chatwoot’s handling of regulated customer data plus its outbound integrations creates a plausible compliance gap if deployed without policy controls.
conditions: IF customer messages or profiles include regulated personal data, retention and export controls must be enforced.
IF chatwoot integrations transmit customer data across jurisdictions, residency review is required.
mitigations: Review data retention settings in chatwoot.
Confirm jurisdiction of each enabled integration.
Minimize stored customer fields.
Publish a deletion/export workflow.
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing.
